Completed the acquired-image spatial-chain pilot: differentiating source trilinear interpolation and residual composition passes all three declared directional-derivative criteria, while the unchanged production gradient fails all three. All 24 previous production/finite-difference/loss/intensity-chain measurements reproduce exactly. Both arms cover all 149,166 nonzero intensity derivatives with zero unavailable derivatives and zero source-grid knots. At epsilon 0.002 mm, symmetric relative errors in percent are production 9.6975 / 16.0727 / 4.4850 versus spatial chain 0.083729 / 0.0025524 / 0.0003653 for translation / smooth-wave / negative-production-gradient. All spatial directions have the required three-point decreasing-error region; the same 0.005 minimum-error criterion is retained.

This supports a concrete spatial-gradient correction: production differences already-warped images, whereas candidate updates compose residual maps and then interpolate source images. The diagnostic differentiates those operations separately in physical coordinates. It does not alter fitting or establish anatomical benefit; the original negative gradient is already a descent direction on this checkpoint. Translation retains finite error and the curves are not monotonic over the whole epsilon range. Other acquired-image states/scales, image order, boundary conditions, applicable regularization and a controlled optimizer/anatomy experiment remain required.

Seven focused tests pass on each of JVM and Scala.js (four new interpolation/composition tests plus three objective tests); runner compilation passes. The first scalar-rank compile error is retained. docs/benchmarks/halfflow-spatial-chain-v1.md links the complete 26-file evidence inventory, visually reviewed plot and verified 14-file source patch against D01. Numerical source a3827bfdff07a34f5c54f5229ab92b515b1b20bf45fbf80751baa228c3f7afaf; diagnostic time 334.74 s is excluded from performance comparisons. D01 and D02 remain incomplete. Evidence stays local pending the requested specific publication approval.
